contributions.detail: Form A is a completely EMPTY grid - not one of its ~17 data rows carries a character - and its printed TOTAL CONTRIBUTIONS cell renders as the accounting dash '-', exactly as the cover's THIS REPORT cell does. On this typed, spreadsheet-generated form the dash is the accounting-format rendering of ZERO, not a nil mark, and the balance chain proves it: 16,875.51 + 0 - 5,221.00 = 11,654.51 exactly, which only closes if contributions THIS is 0. Rows-sum 0 therefore equals both the schedule total and cover line 1 THIS. It does NOT equal the CUMULATIVE cell 16,875.51 (money raised in earlier reports), so this schedule is PER-PERIOD: scope 'period', a different scope from the CUMULATIVE figure the module publishes - honest, not a failure. NOTE the form generation difference: this modern county-branded cover has only THREE lines and NO '$50.00 or less' aggregate line at all, so cover_le50_* are null (the field does not exist), not blank.

expenditures.detail: All 5 typed Form B rows sum to exactly 5,221.00 = the sheet's printed TOTAL EXPENDITURES = the cover's expense THIS REPORT cell = the cover's expense CUMULATIVE cell (three anchors, all agreeing). The expense LAST REPORT cell is left EMPTY, so THIS and CUMULATIVE coincide on this side and the scope is recorded 'cumulative' with that coincidence stated. Contrast the contributions side of the SAME cover, whose LAST cell carries 16,875.51 - a single filing can sit on different scopes side by side, which is why the scope test is run per side.
